newsitem.title: USA: U.S. banks seen in "steady" earnings trend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. banks seen in "steady" earnings trend.

text.p: Third-quarter earnings of U.S. banks which begin appearing in about a week are likely to show "a very steady performance," said Keefe Bruyette & Woods Inc analyst David Berry.
Other analysts were expecting a fairly uneventful crop of quarterly reports. "Pretty good, not too controversial," was the way Moshe Orenbuch of Sanford C. Bernstein Co summed it up.
Loan growth has slowed in the second half from the first half, Orenbuch said, but interest margins are stable to up slightly.

George Salem, analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison, said fundamenetal trends will be very similar to those in the second quarter of 1996. "Loan growth should slow a bit to a mid single-digit annual rate, net interest margins are expected to be flat, expenses seem to be well in control, trading results should be somewhat weaker, and share buybacks continue to be very strong," Salem said in a recent update.

But he also said credit card loan quality will be a focus again this quarter. He said the major issuers of credit cards have experienced further deterioration in credit cards. Net loan losses are likely to increase by 30-50 basis points, he said. In fact, he believes the losses will be increasing through 1997.
In a report several weeks ago, Salem said among major banking companies active in credit cards his greatest concerns were First Chicago NBD Corp and Columbus, Ohio-based Banc One Corp.

Salem rates First Chicago NBD and BancOne a hold. While he does not offically track the four "monoline" companies whose main business is issuance of credit cards, he said he would avoid the group. The monolines are Advanta Corp, Capital One Financial Corp, First USA Inc and MBNA Corp.

Analyst Berry believes that writeoffs for credit card losses will be higher but the rate of increase will slow. "The larger issuers are managing the credit better" with measures such as higher late fees, he said.

The third-quarter earnings of Charlotte, N.C.-based NationsBank Corp will get a close going-over from traders and arbitragers. In late August, NationsBank announced a deal to acquire St. Louis-based Boatmen's Bancshares Inc for about $9 billion in cash and stock.

Boatmen's has the right to walk away from the deal if NationsBank's stock falls more than 20 percent from the 92-5/8 price where it traded the day before the announcement of the deal. Despite a decline right after the deal was announced, the NationsBank stock recently had been trading in the high 80's, substantially above the 74 area that would allow Boatmen's to get out of the deal.
As of now, analysts are anticipating "solid" earnings growth from NationsBank, as one recently put it, or nothing to rock the Boatmen's deal.

According to the data in the First Call tracking service, The consensus estimate for NationsBank's third-quarter is $2.05 per share, up 3.5 percent from $1.98 in the second quarter of 1996 and up up 6.2 percent from $1.93 in the third quarter of 1995.
As is the case with many banks, NationsBank's earnings per share will get a boost from share repurchases, analysts noted.

Among the money center banks, J.P. Morgan & Co Inc is expected to take a charge of around $0.30 per share for costs of starting up a technology alliance which is aimed at controlling outlays for technology. Adding back that charge, analyst Raphael Soifer of Brown Brothers Harriman expects earnings of around $1.55 per share, lower than the $1.78 per share reported for the third quarter of 1995. The results would be beneath the first and second quarters of 1996, $2.13 per share and $2.14 per share respectively, when robust mergers and acquisitions activity, investment banking and exceptionally strong trading results boosted the earnings. "We're expecting M&A to continue to be good, investment banking will be good but maybe not quite as as strong in the second quarter, and trading should be down," Soifer said. Some Wall Street estimates for J.P. Morgan on an operating basis are higher. The highest estimate in the Institutional Brokers Estimate System service is $1.90 per share.
The two-biggest U.S. banks, Citicorp and Chase Manhattan Corp are expected to report earnings October 15, a day on which traders will be inundated with bank earnings.
J.P. Morgan, Jacksonville, Fla.-based Barnett Banks Inc and Atlanta-based SunTrust Banks Inc traditionally get a jump on the pack releasing their quarterly results several days earlier.
